questions.stem:
Statements: I. A severe cold wave swept across the northern plains throughout January this year.
II. Demand for woollen garments and portable room heaters surged in city markets.
Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between the two statements?

options.option_text: Statement I is the cause and Statement II is its effect
Statement II is the cause and Statement I is its effect
Both I and II are independent causes with no causal link
Both I and II are effects of a common independent cause

questions.explanation: A is correct. The cold wave (Statement I) directly caused people to seek warmth, driving up demand for winter items (Statement II). Sequence: extreme cold → consumer need → market surge. Option B fails because a surge in heater sales cannot produce a cold wave — that reverses natural logic. Option D fails because there is no unstated hidden cause; Statement I is itself the direct trigger. Step-by-step: Cold wave hits → Temperatures drop sharply → People require protection → Demand for woollen and heating products rises.

questions.stem:
Statements: I. The state government launched a scheme providing free nutritious mid-day meals to all government primary school students.
II. Student enrolment and daily attendance in government primary schools improved significantly within three months.
Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between the two statements?

options.option_text: Statement I is the cause and Statement II is its effect
Statement II is the cause and Statement I is its effect
Both I and II are independent causes with no causal link
Both I and II are effects of a common independent cause

questions.explanation: A is correct. The mid-day meal scheme (Statement I) gave low-income families a tangible incentive to send children to school, directly causing the rise in attendance and enrolment (Statement II). This is a well-documented policy outcome seen in multiple Indian states. Option B is impossible — improved attendance cannot retroactively cause a government to design and launch a scheme. Option D fails because no third factor is driving both; the scheme is the explicit, stated trigger. Logic chain: Scheme launched → Families incentivised → Children attend regularly → Attendance figures improve.

questions.stem:
Statements: I. Several private coaching institutes for competitive examinations in the city have permanently closed down this year.
II. The central government launched free live-class portals for competitive exam preparation last year.
Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between the two statements?

options.option_text: Statement I is the cause and Statement II is its effect
Statement II is the cause and Statement I is its effect
Both I and II are independent causes with no causal link
Both I and II are effects of a common independent cause

questions.explanation: B is correct. The government's free live-class portals (Statement II, launched last year) created a free alternative that drew students away from paid coaching, causing institutes to lose revenue and shut down (Statement I, this year). The temporal clues 'last year' vs 'this year' confirm II preceded I. Option A is impossible — institutes shutting down cannot cause the government to create online portals. The common temptation is Option C (independent), but the direct competitive displacement of paid coaching by free digital platforms is a well-established mechanism. Logic: Free portal launched → Students switch to free option → Private institutes lose enrolments → Closure.

questions.stem:
Statements: I. Retail prices of onions have crossed ₹80 per kg in major city markets this month.
II. Onion cultivation area in key producing states fell sharply last season due to prolonged drought.
Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between the two statements?

options.option_text: Statement I is the cause and Statement II is its effect
Statement II is the cause and Statement I is its effect
Both I and II are independent causes with no causal link
Both I and II are effects of a common independent cause

questions.explanation: B is correct. The drought-driven fall in cultivation area (Statement II, last season) reduced total supply arriving in markets this season, pushing retail prices to ₹80/kg (Statement I, this month). Temporal sequence confirms II came first. The classic error is choosing A — assuming high retail prices caused less cultivation — but prices spiked because supply fell, not the other way around. Option D is also tempting: one might say 'drought caused both', but Statement II already names drought as its own reason, so drought is not an unstated common cause. Logic chain: Drought → Lower sown area → Less harvest → Reduced market arrivals → Price surge.

questions.stem:
Statements: I. The number of registered vehicles in the metropolitan city has grown by 25% over the past two years.
II. The city's road-widening and flyover projects have stalled due to persistent budget shortfalls over the same two years.
Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between the two statements?

options.option_text: Statement I is the cause and Statement II is its effect
Statement II is the cause and Statement I is its effect
Both I and II are independent causes with no causal link
Both I and II are effects of a common independent cause

questions.explanation: D is correct. Neither statement directly causes the other. Vehicle registrations rising (I) does not drain road-construction budgets (II), and stalled flyover projects do not cause people to buy more cars. Both are parallel outcomes of a common backdrop: rapid, unplanned urbanisation. As a metro city expands fast, commuting needs rise → more vehicles are purchased (I); simultaneously municipal revenues are outpaced by infrastructure demand → budgets run short (II). The trap is Option C (independent/coincidental), which is wrong because the link via urbanisation is real and specific, making D more precise. Examiner note: 'related theme' is not the same as 'cause-effect' — here both statements share an upstream cause but neither causes the other.

questions.stem:
Statements: I. A leading pharmaceutical company has been directed by the drug regulator to immediately recall a specific antibiotic batch from all retail and hospital channels.
II. Multiple patients in different hospitals across two states reported severe adverse reactions after consuming tablets from that antibiotic batch.
Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between the two statements?

options.option_text: Statement I is the cause and Statement II is its effect
Statement II is the cause and Statement I is its effect
Both I and II are independent causes with no causal link
Both I and II are effects of a common independent cause

questions.explanation: B is correct. Patients suffering adverse reactions (Statement II) triggered hospital reporting, regulatory investigation, and ultimately the recall directive (Statement I). The temporal logic is decisive: patients react first → hospitals report → regulator orders recall. The most seductive wrong answer is A — students read I before II and assume the printed order reflects time order, concluding the recall caused the reactions. But a recall directive issued today cannot cause reactions that happened and were reported earlier. Option D is wrong because there is no unstated common cause — the contaminated batch is mentioned in both statements and the reactions are the documented cause of the recall, not a co-effect of something else. Key rule: always ask 'which event MUST logically have occurred first?' — adverse reactions (II) must precede the recall order (I).

questions.stem:
Statements: I. India's central agencies procured a record quantity of wheat at minimum support price this season.
II. The per-hectare wheat yield across major growing states rose by 18% compared to the previous season.
Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between the two statements?

options.option_text: Statement I is the cause and Statement II is its effect
Statement II is the cause and Statement I is its effect
Both I and II are independent causes with no causal link
Both I and II are effects of a common independent cause

questions.explanation: B is correct. The 18% rise in per-hectare yield (Statement II) expanded total output, so more grain was available for farmers to offer at MSP centres — enabling the record procurement (Statement I). The most tempting wrong answer is D (both are effects of a good monsoon). While monsoon may have aided yield, Statement II explicitly names the yield figure as the outcome — it is itself an intermediate result. Choosing D means denying that higher yield directly enables higher procurement, which contradicts basic agricultural economics. Option A (record procurement caused yield to rise) is also impossible — MSP procurement happens after harvest and cannot retroactively improve productivity. Logic chain: Better growing conditions → Yield rises 18% (II) → Total output increases → More surplus offered at MSP centres → Record procurement (I). Distinguish II-causes-I from D: D requires an unstated cause doing the work; here Statement II is the stated and sufficient cause.
